## Upgrading to 5.2

### Changes that do not announce themselves

- **A `.vpl` file opened from a URL reads the files it names from its own
  server.** Its paths used to be resolved against the current directory of
  the machine running it. They are now resolved against the `.vpl` file's
  URL, the way a web page resolves its links: in
  `https://example.org/pipelines/p.vpl`, `style.json` is
  `https://example.org/pipelines/style.json` and `/data/x.csv` is
  `https://example.org/data/x.csv`. Such a pipeline can no longer read a
  local file, so one that named local files has to be run from a local copy,
  and a parameter that needs a local file (a GDAL input, `cutline`,
  `ssh_identity`, a Shapefile) cannot be used in it.

### Pipelines

- **Files can come from a URL.** These parameters take an `http`, `https` or
  `sftp` URL besides a path: `from_csv filename`, `from_geo filename`
  (GeoJSON and line-delimited GeoJSON), `from_tile filename`,
  `vector_update_properties data_source_path`, `vector_reduce_to_style style`,
  `raster_mask geojson`, and `meta_update`'s `tilejson_file`,
  `tilejson_update_file` and `vector_layers_file`. The file is fetched once,
  whole, when the pipeline is built, and the log says when and how large.
  - A remote file is held in memory; an `http` or `https` response over
    256 MB is refused unless `VERSATILES_MAX_HTTP_BODY_BYTES` allows more.
  - Where the format comes from the extension (`from_geo`, `from_tile`), it
    is taken from the URL's last path segment. A URL without one is refused,
    and so is a Shapefile behind a URL.
  - A password in the URL is used and left out of every message.
  - `versatiles convert --dry-run` and editors check the URL's form only;
    whether it answers shows when the pipeline is built.
- The operation metadata reports these parameters as "path or URL" instead
  of "path". An editor that offers a file dialog for them should offer a text
  field as well.

### Rust library

- `versatiles_pipeline`: the parameter types are renamed after what they
  take, which `VPLFieldMeta::rust_type` reports: `SourceLocation` is
  `ContainerLocation`, `GeoDataPath` is `GeoDataLocation`, `TileFilePath` is
  `TileFileLocation`, and the parameters listed above are `FileLocation`.
  `PipelineReader::open_data`, `open_str`, `from_pipeline` and `from_parts`
  take `dir: impl Into<DataLocation>` instead of `&Path`; a `&Path` still
  works. New: `CsvReader::from_input`.
- `versatiles_geometry`: new `feature_source::SourceInput`, a local path or a
  file in memory, with `CsvSourceBuilder::from_input` and
  `GeoJsonSource::from_input`.
- `versatiles_container`: new `open_url_reader`, which opens an `http`,
  `https` or `sftp` URL as a `DataReader`.
- `versatiles_core`: new provided method `DataReaderTrait::url`, the URL a
  reader reads.
